notes: Eclipse Loop 1.7.0 The biggest batch since 1.0. Three themes: the pad grid became a real instrument, the piano roll grew the expression and scale tools it was missing, and the arranger/mixer closed a set of DAW gaps. The pad grid is an instrument now - Pads own samples. Drop a WAV on any pad to give that pad its own sound — a kit can come from sixteen different files instead of sixteen slices of one loop. "Load Sample…" is in the pad right-click menu too. - Click a pad to edit it in the big waveform. Trim, chop and process a pad with the same tools the loop uses. Pad 1 is always the loop, in every pattern, so the way back is spatial rather than buried in a menu. - MUTATE turns one sample into sixteen playable variations — chops drawn from anywhere in the file, pitched, reversed, stretched, stuttered or filtered. Some pads always stay clean, pitches come from musical intervals skewed downward, and the kit is a seeded plan: re-roll for a new one, or recover one you liked. One undo step for the whole kit. - KIT sorts chops by what they are rather than when they happened — kicks on 1-4, snares 5-8, hats 9-12, the rest 13-16 — so the grid is finger-drummable and the same pad means the same kind of sound every time. - The four-click beat: CHOP → KIT → AI DRUMS. KIT names the pads KICK/SNARE/HAT and AI DRUMS reads exactly those names, so one sample becomes a programmed beat. - KEY LOCK means what it says. Tuned samples land in key as they load, so a kit built from four sources is in tune with the loop. Drums are left alone — the detector refuses to name a note for percussive or noisy material. - Rename pads and SEQ tracks (right-click → Rename). Functional, not cosmetic: AI DRUMS maps drum roles by track name. - Note repeat (RPT) picks its division — 1/4 through 1/32 with triplets — and keeps time. It used to run 6.7% fast at 120 BPM and 16% fast at 174. - Chops follow their loop. Pattern A-D swaps the chops with the audio and the notes, and hand-placed slice edges survive the switch. Piano roll - Expression lanes — pitch-bend and CC under the roll, breakpoint editing with glide, captured live by REC MIDI, saved with the project. - Scale highlighting and note names. Five of the thirteen scales silently generated in plain Minor before this — wrong output, not just wrong display. - Velocity lane pinned under the roll; drag across a selection to set it all. - Note chase — dropping the playhead inside a held note re-triggers it, and re-asserts the last bend and CC. - Scroll past bar 4. The roll's width was hardcoded to 16 beats, so notes after bar four were unreachable. The key strip stays pinned now too. - Pattern CHAIN plays A/B/C/D in an order, advancing on the loop wrap. MIDI export/import - Multi-track, with lane names and one channel each. Every export used to flatten to a single track. - Expression curves are written out, and the time signature is correct — every .mid this app had exported carried 4/2. - Import is symmetric: a multi-track .mid from another DAW round-trips. Arranger, mixer and recording - Clip volume envelopes, drawn on the clip body; applied in playback and freeze. - Tempo ramps — accelerando/ritardando between tempo points, integrated over the curve rather than stepped. - Automation runs on the audio thread — block-accurate, and it no longer freezes when the arrange panel is hidden. - Punch in/out with pre-roll, and input-monitor Auto/Off for direct hardware monitoring. - Live recording is visible — pulsing dot, elapsed clock, input meter with peak hold, and a NO INPUT SIGNAL warning after 1.5 s. - PRE/POST-fader sends per row; pre-fader now works in plugin mode too. - 32-bit float export in both bounce dialogs, TPDF dither on every 16-bit write. - NRW narrow strips, IN/OUT picker chevrons, per-track phase invert and input trim, and host latency reporting for plugin use. - Knobs show their values on hover and drag. - Fixed: clicking the left edge of "+ NEW TRACK" collapsed the mixer's inserts/sends/IO sections with no way to bring them back. Docs The quickstart teaches first — it had opened with ten "New in…" sections. Every user-facing control was audited against the manual and the quickstart; BROWSER, Browse MIDI, CUT REGION, DC REM, Scale Lock, Chord Lock, Doubler and the drag-length selector had no coverage at all.
